result.summary:
Fixed all three TEST-RUNNER-attributed root causes. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the dispatch's own premise on fix #2, established by direct investigation before touching anything: the actual `:clone` tenant-provisioning mechanism lives entirely in test/support/tenant_template.ex (Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate), not in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex. That module's own moduledoc says so explicitly ('Production path untouched ... Zero new code is reachable from real tenant onboarding'), and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex itself contains only provision_tenant_schema/1 and replay_migrations/2 (the :replay path) -- grepped directly, no 'clone'/'LIKE'/'INCLUDING ALL' text anywhere in that file. So this rework's diff touches zero lib/letflow/ files; both fixes are in test/support/ and docs/status/.

(1) POLLER STATE (test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs): confirmed via grep that all ~16 hand-built raw state maps (`%{last_retention_run_at: nil}` and `%{last_retention_run_at: nil, last_tick_started_at: nil}` variants) predate poller.ex's REQ-376 addition of a required :last_partition_maintenance_run_at key. Added `last_partition_maintenance_run_at: nil` to every one via sed (verified each site individually afterward), matching exactly how :last_retention_run_at is already initialized elsewhere in the same file. poller.ex itself untouched -- did not weaken it to Map.get/2, per the dispatch's own explicit instruction; the complete-map shape is correct, the fixtures were stale. mix format re-wrapped 5 of the newly-widened lines to stay under the line-length limit.

(2) CLONE-VS-TEMPLATE PARITY (test/support/tenant_template.ex): read do_clone/2 and every one of assert_clone_parity!/2's 13 dimension-check helpers in full. Root cause confirmed exactly as TEST-RUNNER's evidence described: dims #1 (table set) and #3 (constraints) query the reference (template) schema's FULL catalog unconditionally, with no allowance for REQ-376's own, already-established, already-REVIEWER-signed-off design fact (decision 0037's 're-gate 2' section explicitly calls the clone schema 'deliberately-unpartitioned'; test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's own req376_partition_management_table?/1 doc comment and tenant_template.ex's own readd_foreign_keys!/1 and structural_indexdef/1 comments all independently establish the same thing) that a :clone-provisioned tenant's events/events_archive are, by design, plain unpartitioned tables -- CREATE TABLE (LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL) cannot and never could copy PARTITION BY. THIS IS THE REAL FIX, not a whitelist invented for this bug: taught check_table_set/2 (dim #1), constraint_rows/1 (dim #3, used by check_constraints/2), and index_defs/1 (dim #4a, used by check_index_structure/2) to reject rows belonging to the 7 partition-management tables via the SAME Letflow.TenantFixture.req376_partition_management_table?/1 oracle this exact file already trusts at line ~456 (template_self_check!/1, use site 1) and in readd_foreign_keys!/1's own conparentid=0 filter -- consistent application of an already-reviewed oracle across every comparison site, not new logic. check_table_set/2 filters only the `missing` set (not ref_tables/extra directly), specifically so the SAME function still works correctly for use site 1 (assert_template_parity_against_independent_reference!/1, where BOTH sides are genuinely partitioned and a real diff must still be caught) -- verified this distinction was necessary by first shipping the naive ref_tables-level filter, watching it turn use site 1's two tests into false failures (false 'extra' reports), and correcting to the missing-set-only filter, which then passed both use sites cleanly. Also found and fixed a related discovery made only by actually running the test: dimension #12 (check_ruled_out_properties/2) legitimately disagrees on relkind ('p' partitioned vs 'r' ordinary) for events/events_archive themselves -- added a narrow normalize_relkind/1 helper that collapses only that one field, only for those two tables, while leaving every other ruled-out property (relrowsecurity, relforcerowsecurity, relispartition, reltablespace) compared with zero tolerance as before.

(3) STATUS INDEX COUNT (docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml): confirmed via `grep -c "^  - req:" docs/status/requirement_status.v21.yaml` = 20 on-disk entries (REQ-376's own `started` event, appended earlier this run, was the 20th and never bumped the declared count). Bumped volume 21's `entries:` 19 -> 20 with a note following the volume's own convention (composed after the prior 19->20 pattern already established there).

VERIFICATION, all against real Postgres (docker letflow-postgres-1, port 5462):
- test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs: 21/21 passed.
- test/support/tenant_template_test.exs: 7/7 passed (was 4/7 before the fix -- all three prior failures, including the two discovered only by running it, now pass).
- test/support/tenant_template_retry_test.exs + test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs (adjacent :clone-path tests, checked for regression): 5/5 passed.
- test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs: 20/20 passed (A9 included).
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force: 0 warnings.
- mix format --check-formatted: exit 0.

FULL SUITE (TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 scripts/test_parallel.sh, per this host's established override): first attempt aborted -- all 4 partitions exited 127 with no Result: line and no error trace, mid-run (~5 min in, well before either the 48-min historical wall time or the Bash tool's own 10-min single-call cap), consistent in shape with docs/anti-patterns.md's zombie-BEAM-VM entry though the exact trigger here was different (no zombies were left behind afterward -- docker/pg_stat_activity confirmed clean). Also found and killed one genuinely-zombied erl.exe (PID 1050307, application_name letflow_mixtest_26712, 32 held connections, no corresponding live test command) left over from my OWN immediately-prior targeted-test commands, before the first full-suite attempt -- confirmed dead via pg_stat_activity dropping back to idle baseline. Re-launched the second attempt using nohup ... < /dev/null & with the PID persisted to a scratchpad file, and polled to completion via REPEATED SEPARATE blocking Bash tool calls (a bounded while-kill-0 loop per call, each well under the tool's own timeout, chained across calls rather than one long single call or any run_in_background/Monitor wait) -- confirmed empirically that this survives across tool-call boundaries where the first attempt's single embedded nohup-then-poll-in-one-call pattern did not. RESULT, clean, no contamination: `combined: 4626 tests, 6 properties, 0 failures (4632/4632 passed)` -- 0 failures total, including the ~20 TEST-RUNNER filed as pre-existing/environmental connection contention (the other concurrent session on this host, PID 13228 in TEST-RUNNER's report, had exited by the time this run started -- confirmed no other erl.exe processes were alive beforehand). No erl.exe processes remained after completion.
result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (2c) for re-gate (tenant_provisioning.ex :clone path change), then REVIEWER (2d), then back to TEST-RUNNER (4) for final full-suite re-run. NOTE for SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER: as established in this handoff's summary, no lib/letflow/ file was touched this rework -- the actual :clone mechanism lives in test/support/tenant_template.ex (test-only infra, its own moduledoc: 'Production path untouched ... Zero new code is reachable from real tenant onboarding'), not in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex (which implements only :replay). Both changed files (test/support/tenant_template.ex, test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs) are test-only; docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml is a docs bookkeeping fix. Whether this still warrants a full tenant-data-path SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (vs. REVIEWER only) given no production code changed is SECURITY-REVIEWER's/REVIEWER's own call to make, not mine -- flagging the file-location correction rather than silently deciding to skip the gate myself.

issues.description: The dispatch instructions for this rework (and, by extension, TEST-RUNNER's step-04 next_action before it) named lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex as the file needing the :clone-path fix and framed it as production tenant-provisioning code warranting a SECURITY-REVIEWER tenant-data-path gate. Direct investigation (grep, moduledoc reading) established this is factually incorrect: the :clone mechanism is entirely test/support/ infrastructure (Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate), explicitly documented as never reachable from real tenant onboarding. Flagging so the next gate step re-evaluates gate scope against the actual diff rather than the dispatch's original (inaccurate) file-location premise.

A full-suite scripts/test_parallel.sh run launched via a single Bash tool call embedding both the nohup-launch and a blocking while-kill-0 poll loop died silently (all 4 partitions exit 127, no error trace, no zombies left behind) approximately 5 minutes in -- well short of both the historical ~48-minute wall time and the tool's own 10-minute per-call cap, so neither explains it. A second attempt, structurally identical except the launch and each poll interval were issued as separate Bash tool calls (nohup launch with < /dev/null and a persisted PID in one call, then repeated separate bounded poll calls), ran to full clean completion. Recording this here since the mechanism itself was not identified (no crash trace was ever produced) -- worth watching for on this host; if it recurs, launch-and-poll-in-separate-calls is the confirmed-working pattern, not a single combined call.
